title: AccelES: Accelerating Top-K SpMV for Embedding Similarity via Low-bit Pruning
problem: Top-K sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) for recommendation system embedding similarity suffers from high latency due to inefficient memory access patterns when scanning full-precision sparse matrices to identify the most relevant embeddings.
motivation: Real-time recommendation systems require sub-millisecond embedding similarity queries at scale, but existing CPU/GPU/FPGA solutions are bottlenecked by memory bandwidth when performing SpMV over large sparse feature matrices.
method: AccelES employs a two-stage computation scheme: Stage 1 uses a compact low-bit (pruned) representation of the sparse matrix to rapidly identify the top-K candidate entries with minimal data movement, and Stage 2 performs full-precision SpMV only on this pruned candidate subset. Two novel sparse matrix storage formats, Ultra-CSR and Random-CSR, are introduced to optimize memory bandwidth utilization for irregular access patterns inherent in SpMV. The low-bit approximation in Stage 1 filters out irrelevant entries early, reducing the volume of full-precision computation dramatically.
key_novelty: Two-stage low-bit pruning that decouples candidate identification (low-bit/low-cost) from precise scoring (full-precision/selective), enabling asymmetric computation allocation for Top-K SpMV.
contributions: Two-stage Top-K SpMV algorithm combining low-bit candidate selection with full-precision verification
Ultra-CSR and Random-CSR matrix formats optimized for memory bandwidth in sparse embedding lookup
Accelerator achieving 3.4x over FPGA, 2.5x over GPU, and 153.3x over CPU for Top-K SpMV
Demonstrated applicability to real-time recommendation system workloads

metrics.speedup: 3.4x over FPGA, 2.5x over GPU, 153.3x over CPU

limitations: The accuracy impact of the low-bit pruning approximation on final recommendation quality (beyond top-K overlap) is not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Low-bit two-stage pruning for accelerated Top-K sparse embedding similarity
